correctness.rationale: The dimension-two split criterion for distinct functions is proved both ways. In a tree the positive root-version space has positive splits of size at most two and dimension exactly two iff the queried vertex has degree at least three. The negative space admits depth two exactly when the specified closed-neighborhood intersection count lies between two and the complement size minus two. This proves all-order necessity and sufficiency of the dimension-three test. Small trees and the leaf-based dimension-two floor are treated separately. VC dimension at most two follows from uniqueness of the common center for two neighbors in a tree. A separate recursive Littlestone solver checks all unlabeled trees of order at most eight and an explicit depth-three certificate; the computations are not used to infer the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Closed graph neighborhoods and fixed-radius tree balls are natural set systems studied for learning and graph VC computation. This gives a complete sharp online mistake-complexity trichotomy for all finite trees, an O(n^2) geometric recognition test, the smallest depth-three witness of order eight, a complete sharp eight-vertex finite transition (12 of 23 types), and a strict VC-versus-adaptive example. The value is in the structural classification and sharp boundary, not code correctness or alleged generality beyond the stated domain.
